title: Bessel I0 tail gives a sub-exponential MGF for the period law -- a Bennett/Freedman bound the Azuma route could not reach (it used only L^inf increments)
wall: W-Johnson / W-BGK. The Bennett/Freedman tower route collapses to the SAME wall documented in CumulantTowerAzumaWall.lean and docs/kb/deltastar-407-cumulant-deep-nonbetti-verdict-2026-06-13.md. Three independent obstructions, each verified at proper dyadic subgroups (n=16,32,64, beta=4): (1) the tower increments are NOT a mean-zero martingale-difference sequence, so NO martingale concentration (Azuma, Bennett, Freedman, Bernstein) applies at all; (2) at the worst-case (house-achieving) coset the increments add fully coherently, so variance/MGF information is irrelevant; (3) even granting the Bessel conditional variance <S>~n, the L^inf range term (2/3)b_max*ln m that any Bennett/Freedman bound necessarily carries DOMINATES <S>=n by 3.8-5.8x, exactly as the KB stated -- now confirmed with the actual Bessel conditional variance rather than the crude L^inf. The MGF the worst Gauss period actually needs is still governed by the char-p energy E_r^{Fp} to depth r~log q (the BGK/Bourgain-Shkredov sqrt-cancellation wall, CyclotomicNormDefectThreshold vacuous at phi(2^mu)=n/2), unchanged.
evidence: Probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C100_bessel_bennett_tower.py (exact mod-p integer arithmetic for the periods, PROPER dyadic subgroups mu_n with 2^a|p-1, large primes, beta=log_n(p)=4.0 in [4,5] prize regime: n=16 p=65537 m=4096 L=8.32; n=32 p=1048609 m=32769 L=10.40; n=64 p=16777601 m=262150 L=12.48). Three decisive tests on the dyadic tower eta^{(2^a)}_b = sum_k Delta_k(b), Delta_k = eta^{(2^{k-1})}_{b w_{k-1}}: (T1) MARTINGALE PROPERTY FAILS -- a Bennett/Freedman bound requires E[Delta_k | F_{k-1}]=0; measured E[Delta_1]=+1.82,+2.00,+2.00 (level-1 period = 2cos, systematically biased positive at worst directions) and per-level conditional means E[Delta_k | S_{k-1}>0] are NONZERO (-0.07 to -0.92 at n=16, smaller but still nonzero at n=32,64). The increments are not a martingale-difference sequence, so the premise 'feed the conditional MGF into a martingale tail' is void. (T2) WORST COSET FULLY COHERENT -- at the house-achieving b the increment signs are ALL +1 (n=16 b=1; n=32 b=1361; n=64 b=4058) and coherence |S_a|/sum|Delta_k| = 1.000 EXACTLY: the house is built by coherent addition, not random-walk cancellation, so the conditional variance/MGF is precisely the quantity that gives no information -- Bennett/Freedman reduce to the triangle inequality sum B_{k-1} on the worst coset. (T3) RANGE TERM DOMINATES -- the Bessel conditional variance <S>=sum Var(Delta_k) is correctly ~n (ratio 0.82, 0.93, 0.97 -> 1, confirming the Bessel L^2 scale, the one CORRECT claim of the connection), and the Bennett variance-term-alone sqrt(2 L <S>) does track the target sqrt(2 n L) (14.81 vs 16.31; 24.89 vs 25.80; 39.34 vs 39.96). But the full Freedman bound, which must include the range correction (2/3)b_max*L, gives t* = 79.5, 163, 242 -- worse than even Azuma (67, 130, 196) and 4.9-6.3x the target; range/<S> = 5.82, 5.35, 3.81 (>>1, so the L^inf range term dominates the variance term at every prize scale, exactly as docs/kb/deltastar-407-cumulant-deep-nonbetti-verdict says 'b_max*t ~ n ln m dominates <S>=n once ln m>1').
honest_note: Two-sided. CORRECT in C100: the Bessel even-moment law E_r=(2r)![x^r]I0(2sqrt x)^{n/2} with the in-tree bessel_energy_le_gaussian (I0(2x)<=e^{x^2}) does give a sub-Gaussian per-level conditional variance ~n (verified <S>/n -> 1); this is the genuine bulk/L^2 increment scale and is sharper than the crude L^inf bound B_{k-1}~sqrt(n L) that Azuma is forced to use -- so the connection's diagnosis 'Azuma overpays because it uses only L^inf' is accurate, and a pure-variance Bennett term WOULD reach the target if it stood alone. DECISIVELY WRONG / the reason it does not close: a Bennett/Freedman martingale bound is NOT just a variance term -- (a) it requires a mean-zero martingale-difference structure that the tower increments DO NOT have (T1: conditional means nonzero), and (b) it necessarily carries an L^inf range correction (1/3)b_max*t that, with b_max~sqrt(n L) ~ the whole period, scales as n*ln m and DOMINATES the variance <S>=n (T3), and (c) the worst coset that defines the house adds coherently (T2: coherence 1.000), where no concentration inequality beats the triangle inequality regardless of the variance. So coupling the proven Bessel MGF to the proven uncorrelatedness DOES NOT beat the sqrt(2 ln m) Azuma inflation -- it lands on the identical obstruction already formalized in CumulantTowerAzumaWall.lean (azuma_inflates_target, azuma_factor_gt_one) and recorded in the cumulant-deep-nonbetti verdict KB; the assertion that 'coupling the Bessel MGF to uncorrelatedness has not been tried' is the only novel-sounding part and it resolves to the same wall once you note that 2nd-order uncorrelatedness is not a martingale and the worst coset is coherent. NOT a closure, NOT a refutation of a clean claim (so not DISPROOF_LOG material -- it is a route that welds back to the wall, hence OPEN). Caveats: probes use float64 complex exp on exact mod-p integers at modest n,p (prize-scale p~2^256 infeasible); the coherence=1.000 and conditional-mean-nonzero facts reproduce the in-tree probe_407_cumulant_martingale_deep.py findings independently at fresh proper-subgroup primes; I did not build the cited oleans (no lock taken) -- CumulantTowerAzumaWall.lean axiom-cleanliness is asserted by its in-file #print axioms, not re-run here.
